added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  Suppose
\[
 \gamma>s_0
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 d>\frac{2s_0\gamma}{\gamma-s_0}.
\]
Then the dimension condition implies \(d>2s_0\), and there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \ge c n^{\kappa},
 \qquad
 \kappa=
 \frac{2\gamma}{4\gamma+d}
 -\frac{2s_0}{2s_0+d}
 =\frac{2\{d(\gamma-s_0)-2s_0\gamma\}}
 {(4\gamma+d)(2s_0+d)}>0.
\]
Consequently \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\to\infty\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: A necessary-and-sufficient equality region, the order of the radius ratio throughout the complementary regimes, and all unresolved boundary logarithms.
open_obligations.obstruction: The sparse converse and known-propensity benchmark now prove strict polynomial divergence in one explicit region, but the observational lower and upper maps remain unmatched outside the proved no-penalty region. Therefore they do not determine necessity, the exact threshold boundary, or the remaining complementary regimes.
open_obligations.attempted: Combined the same-class sparse nuisance lower bound with the known-propensity upper bound, verified that the strict dimension condition implies the sparse-regime hypothesis, and optimized the resulting exponent algebraically. Per the final-maximality directive, no new upper architecture was attempted.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  Two sufficient regions are proved on the unchanged class.  First,
\[
 s_0\ge\gamma\quad\text{and}\quad d\le4\gamma
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}.
\]
At \(d=4\gamma\), this comparison gives \(n^{-1/4}\) without a logarithm.  Second, if
\[
 \gamma>s_0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 d>\frac{2s_0\gamma}{\gamma-s_0},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \ge c n^{\frac{2\gamma}{4\gamma+d}-\frac{2s_0}{2s_0+d}}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The necessary-and-sufficient equality region is not yet established.  In particular, the regimes \(s_0\ge\gamma\) with \(d>4\gamma\), and \(\gamma>s_0\) with \(d\le 2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\), including the equality boundary and any transition logarithms there, remain unresolved.

prose_updates.tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational radius satisfies the proved all-regime upper bound \(\rho_n^*\le Cb_n\) and, for \(d\ge2s_0\), the original fixed-sample lower bound \(\rho_n^*\ge c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The no-penalty region \(s_0\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\) remains matched.  A strict penalty is now proved whenever \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\): then \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\to\infty\).  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the exponent is at least \(4/35\).  The complete frontier and its remaining transition boundaries are open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures and adjacent minimax results do not give the fixed-sample critical radius or the exact value-of-known-propensity frontier on this binary exact-uniform class.  The direct-Hellinger construction determines a nuisance-driven converse for \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\), and comparison with the known-propensity benchmark proves strict divergence when \(\gamma>\alpha+\beta\) and \(d>2(\alpha+\beta)\gamma/(\gamma-\alpha-\beta)\).  The best proved observational upper map still does not match the converse outside the no-penalty region, so necessity and the transition boundaries remain unresolved.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies an explicit total profiled fourth-order test and all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark and matched no-penalty region, and a same-class fixed-\(n\) lower construction giving \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) whenever \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\).  Combining that converse with the known-propensity benchmark yields the explicit polynomial lower bound \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) throughout the proved strict-penalty region, without claiming that this sufficient region is necessary or that the complete frontier is solved.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class: its pointwise-estimation model is larger and its binary lower submodel uses a support with holes.  The converse here uses the localized fuzzy-hypothesis idea only after proving exact full-cube uniform masses, componentwise binary margins, a common sign-conditioned singleton predictive law, and a bounded-overlap connected-graph Hellinger calculation.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing under a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-covariance validity and spline power under common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, gives asymptotic structured-rule homogeneity results under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance.  None supplies the componentwise constant-null fixed-sample nuisance lower map proved here, the resulting explicit sufficient strict-divergence region for unknown versus known propensity, or an omnibus test that closes the remaining same-class frontier.

statement_notes.gap: The unchanged-class comparison now proves equality on the sufficient region \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\), and strict polynomial divergence on the sufficient region \(\gamma>\alpha+\beta\), \(d>2(\alpha+\beta)\gamma/(\gamma-\alpha-\beta)\).  A necessary-and-sufficient partition, the remaining ratio orders, and unresolved boundary logarithms are still open.
